Column-supported embankment. 6-1
figures.description: Description Embankments over soft, compressible soils (peat, very soft clay, organic deposits) where strict settlement limits apply or conventional ground improvement is insufficient. Vertical columns beneath a load transfer platform (LTP) support embankments over soft/compressible soils System transfers embankment loads through LTP to columns, bypassing weak subgrade Common column types: driven piles, auger-cast piles, CMC, deep mixed columns, vibro-concrete columns LTP typically granular fill with one or more geosynthetic reinforcement layers Applicable where settlement must be minimized and conventional ground improvement is inadequate Allows embankments over peat, very soft clay, and highly compressible soils

figures.caption: Column-supported embankment with geosynthetic reinforcement. 6-2
figures.description: Design Concepts Design of load transfer platform, column layout, and geosynthetic reinforcement for CSE systems. Three design components: column design, load transfer platform design, and geosynthetic reinforcement design Load transfer efficiency (LTE) = fraction of embankment load carried by columns vs. subgrade Design methods: BS 8006 (arching), EBGEO (Germany), Hewlett & Randolph (1988) arch mechanism Geosynthetic reinforcement provides tensile resistance to maintain LTP arch and limit differential settlement Typical LTP thickness 0.6–1.2 m; primary variables are column spacing, diameter, LTP thickness No dedicated AASHTO LRFD specification yet; most designs use allowable stress with engineering judgment

figures.caption: New Jersey Light Rail project. 6-5
figures.description: Load Transfer Platform and Geosynthetic Reinforcement Design of granular LTP and geosynthetic reinforcement for load transfer in CSE systems. LTP: compacted granular fill (phi >= 35°) above column heads; minimum height H >= 0.7*(s-d) Geosynthetic (geogrid or woven geotextile) placed at base or mid-height of LTP Geosynthetic provides tensile membrane support between column heads Required tensile strength depends on column spacing, head size, embankment geometry, and settlement limits Typical geosynthetic strengths: 100–400 kN/m for CSE applications Multiple geosynthetic layers may be used for larger spans or higher loads

figures.caption: CSE with column caps. 6-16
figures.description: Construction Construction planning, sequencing, and quality control for column-supported embankment systems. Construction sequence: site prep → columns → pile caps → LTP fill → geosynthetic → LTP fill → embankment Working platform (0.5–1.0 m compacted granular fill) required before column installation on soft subgrade Column QC: extraction testing, integrity testing, or load testing Embankment fill should be staged if lateral failure of soft subgrade is possible Column batter or lateral analysis required for high embankments with steep slopes Geosynthetic seams must be oriented perpendicular to embankment axis (or as designed)
